name: Jira Cloud

auth.keyHelp: Create an API token (it acts as you; read-only needs a scoped token with read:jira-work and read:jira-user).

read.label: List an issue's available status changes

write.label: Move an issue to another status

notes: Paths, parameters and OAuth scopes were read from Atlassian's official OpenAPI file (swagger-v3.v3.json) because the REST doc pages are script-rendered. Basic auth: account email as username, API token as password, sent as 'Authorization: Basic base64(email:token)'. IMPORTANT: the old GET/POST /rest/api/3/search are flagged in the spec as being removed; use GET /rest/api/3/search/jql (token pagination via nextPageToken; the JQL must be bounded). Unscoped API tokens are used against the site URL ({site}). Scoped API tokens are instead called through https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudId}, a different baseUrl this manifest does not model; how to look up the cloudId was not in the pages read. A truly read-only key is only possible with a scoped token (spec scopes read:jira-work, read:jira-user); an unscoped token inherits all of the user's rights. Create issue needs a 'fields' object (project, summary, issuetype); comment and description bodies are Atlassian Document Format on API v3. Official Atlassian Rovo MCP server is https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp (OAuth 2.1; an org admin can enable API-token auth: Basic base64(email:token) for a personal token with scopes, or Bearer for a service-account key); it covers Jira, Confluence and more.
